# multi-modal-jev-browser

A browser agent where a small decision model picks each action and a vision LLM steps in only when it is unsure.
CLI, Python library and MCP server.

## Read these, in this order

- README.md: what it is, quick start, MCP setup, the model table, limits, safety
- AGENTS.md: written for an AI agent pointed at the repo. Tools with examples, environment variables, how to run the tests, the three common failures
- docs/design.md: why each rule exists and the failure behind it
- docs/extending.md: the four extension points with a complete worked example each
- skills/browse/SKILL.md: how to use the browse tool from a Claude Code session
- examples/: MCP config for Claude Code, opencode, Cursor and a generic mcpServers file
- examples/bench.py, examples/compare_deciders.py, examples/make_demo_gif.py: the benchmark, the three way comparison and the demo GIF

## Run it in one line

```bash
uvx --from git+https://github.com/foklepoint/multi-modal-jev-browser mmjb-mcp
```

## Check the setup

```bash
uvx --from git+https://github.com/foklepoint/multi-modal-jev-browser mmjb doctor
```

## Run the tests

```bash
uv run pytest -q
```

## Key ideas

- One decision-model call per step. It answers typed multiple-choice and yes/no questions about the page.
- The element numbers in the element list are the numbers drawn on the numbered screenshot.
- DONE and BLOCKED are yes/no questions, never items in the operation menu.
- A DONE claim is only accepted when the page shows confirmation text that was not there before, or a
  yes/no question about the new text scores 0.9 or above. The agent never reloads to prove a goal.
- A click that opens a new tab moves the agent to that tab and says so in the step record.
- `allow_writes` is false by default. Nothing is typed and no submit button is clicked until it is on.
- Page text is untrusted data, never instructions.

## Outcomes

`verified`, `unverified`, `blocked`, `step_limit`, `error`. Exit codes 0, 3, 2, 4, 1.
